name: Magnolia Oil & Gas Corporation

profile.description: Magnolia Oil & Gas is a Houston-based independent E&P focused on South Texas — the Giddings field (Austin Chalk/Eagle Ford) and Karnes County. Founded in 2018 by former Occidental CEO Steve Chazen and led since September 2022 by CEO (and since July 2025 Chairman) Christopher Stavros, it runs a low-reinvestment, free-cash-flow-and-dividend model. On September 10, 2026 it closed the ~$4.1B acquisition of WildFire Energy (~810,000 net Giddings acres plus a sand mine), lifting Q4 2026 production guidance to 159-161 Mboe/d from 106.1 Mboe/d in Q2 2026 and raising the quarterly dividend 9% to $0.18. Shares outstanding ~267M; pre-deal market cap roughly $6.7-6.9B.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Magnolia's model has been consistent — 'appraise, acquire, grow, and further exploit' in Giddings since inception — culminating in the ~$4.1B WildFire acquisition; this is a scaling of the existing business, not a new revenue stream [2][5]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI deployment or quantified AI savings were found in filings or interviews. Market Share (1/2): With WildFire's ~810,000 net acres Magnolia becomes the leading Giddings operator, but it remains a price-taker in a commodity market [2]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Development visibility is specific — Q4 2026 production guided to 159-161 Mboe/d with ~$235M of Q4 D&C — but this is drilling inventory rather than new products [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Magnolia reports no R&D expense [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Magnolia's stated purpose centers on disciplined capital allocation, a low reinvestment rate and returning free cash flow to shareholders — a financial operating model interchangeable with other returns-focused E&Ps rather than a purpose beyond profit [5]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable or community investment programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found for its ~262 employees [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful insider open-market purchases were identified in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (12 weight units). D/E ~52% (derived pro forma: ~$2.15B gross debt from $400M legacy notes + $600M assumed notes + ~$490M new notes + ~$660M revolver, against equity of ~$4.1B after the share issuance; Yahoo's pre-deal figure is 19.2%) scores 1.0 [1][2][4]. ROE 20.85% scores 1.0 [4]. Revenue growth YoY 50.1% scores 1.0 [4]. Revenue 5yr CAGR 19.4% (derived from FMP: $541.3M in 2020 to $1,311.8M in 2025, flattered by the 2020 trough) scores 1.0 [3]. Forward P/E 7.99 scores 1.0 [4]. Profit margin 28.77% scores 1.0 [4]. Payout ratio 27.6% scores 1.0 [4]. Consecutive years paid 6 (dividends since 2021) scores 0.6 (2x) [4]. Consecutive years of growth 5 (annual totals $0.08, $0.40, $0.46, $0.52, $0.60, and 2026 on track above $0.60) scores 0.5 [4]. Dividend growth CAGR 14.5% (derived from 2022-2025 annual totals, as a full 5-year base is not meaningful) scores 1.0 (2x) [4]. Weighted sum 10.7 / 12 → 8.92 → 9. Yield 2.87% uses the new $0.18 quarterly rate annualized ($0.72) on $25.05 [2]. Liquidity passes: 3.79M × $25.05 ≈ $95M/day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Magnolia extracts and sells physical oil and gas; no AI tool can substitute for hydrocarbon production, and our searches found no analyst commentary flagging AI as a threat to its earnings [2][5]. AI-driven data-center power demand is, if anything, supportive of natural gas demand, while the main risks are commodity prices and integration. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue or quantified AI efficiency gains were identified.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Magnolia is a well-run finite player. Its organizing idea — spend a fraction of cash flow, grow modestly, return the rest — is a financial discipline, not a Just Cause. It handled CEO succession smoothly and has evolved within South Texas, but the $4.1B WildFire deal is a bet on scale in the same basin, and nothing in its communications speaks to a future state beyond shareholder returns.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): Magnolia's stated purpose is a capital-allocation model — a low reinvestment rate, steady production growth and free cash flow returned to shareholders (e.g., 2022 D&C spending of just 34% of adjusted EBITDAX, $824M FCF) — which is a finite, shareholder-return objective rather than a vision of a better future [5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is solid — Stavros was CFO from inception and succeeded founder Steve Chazen through planned succession in 2022, then became Chairman in July 2025 — and the ~262-person organization shows no cultural red flags, but no retention or empowerment evidence was found [4][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary referencing learning from competitors was found; competitive language centers on acquiring acreage and returns [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Magnolia has shifted its center of gravity from Karnes toward the Giddings field and now into a much larger Giddings position plus a sand mine, an evolution within its existing oil-and-gas model rather than a transformation [2][5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership has held to spending discipline through commodity cycles rather than chasing volume, and the $4.1B WildFire acquisition was a major long-horizon commitment to Giddings inventory and vertical integration (owned sand supply) [2][5]. Whether it serves anything beyond scale is unclear.

investment_thesis: Magnolia is a disciplined, high-margin Giddings consolidator. TTM profit margin is 28.8%, ROE 20.9%, and the stock trades at 11.0x trailing and 8.0x forward earnings, with Yahoo showing revenue up 50.1% and earnings up 136.6% in the latest reported quarter year over year [4]. The ~$4.1B WildFire Energy acquisition (closed September 10, 2026) adds ~810,000 net Giddings acres and a sand mine supplying ~80% of Magnolia's sand needs, with management targeting more than $100M of annual synergies and guiding Q4 2026 production to 159-161 Mboe/d — roughly 50% above Q2's 106.1 Mboe/d [1][2]. Pro forma net debt of ~$1.9B is below 1.0x 2027E EBITDA at strip, and the board raised the quarterly dividend 9% to $0.18 alongside the deal [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that Magnolia just abandoned the conservative balance sheet that defined it. The deal was funded with $2.65B of cash (revolver draws, new senior notes, a ~$1-1.2B equity offering), 32.2M new shares to WildFire, and $600M of assumed 7.5% notes — taking net debt from near zero to ~$1.9B and the share count to ~267M [1][2]. One-time transaction and integration costs of $65-75M hit Q3 2026, and Q4 D&C spending steps up to ~$235M [1]. As an oil-weighted producer (49-50% oil), earnings remain fully exposed to commodity prices — FY2025 revenue was flat at $1.31B and net income fell to $325M from $366M before 2026 price gains [3]. The 2026 proxy also discloses routine flaring on properties acquired in 2023 that is inconsistent with company standards, now being remediated [5].
key_catalysts: WildFire integration: delivery of the targeted >$100M of annual cost savings and synergies and Q4 2026 production of 159-161 Mboe/d [1][2]
Q3 2026 results on November 5, 2026 — first look at combined free cash flow and the pace of debt reduction from ~$1.9B net debt [1]
Dividend growth: the 9% raise to $0.18/quarter (an annualized $0.72) extends five consecutive years of per-share increases, with buybacks possible once leverage normalizes [2]
key_risks: Leverage and integration: net debt rose to ~$1.9B with $600M of assumed 7.5% notes and new senior notes; a commodity downturn during integration would pressure the dividend and buyback capacity [1][2]
Commodity exposure: oil is ~49-50% of volumes, so the 50% YoY revenue and 137% earnings growth in the latest quarter can reverse quickly with crude prices — FY2025 revenue was flat at $1.31B [3][4]
Dilution and execution: ~81M additional shares (equity offering plus 32.2M to WildFire) mean per-share growth requires the acquired acreage to perform as underwritten [1][2]
